@[reducible, simp]
def can_jump_precond (nums : List Nat) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  0 < nums.length ∧
  nums.length ≤ 10000 ∧
  (∀ i, i < nums.length → nums.getD i 0 ≤ 10000)
  -- !benchmark @end precond

def is_valid_jump_path (path : List Nat) (nums : List Nat) : Prop :=
  path.length > 0 ∧
  path.head? = some 0 ∧
  path.getLast? = some (nums.length - 1) ∧
  (∀ i, i < path.length → path.getD i 0 < nums.length) ∧
  (∀ i, i < path.length - 1 →
    let u := path.getD i 0
    let v := path.getD (i+1) 0
    u < v ∧ v ≤ u + nums.getD u 0)

-- !benchmark @start auxcode
@[reducible]
def is_path_from (nums : List Nat) (k : Nat) (p : List Nat) : Prop :=
  0 < p.length ∧
  p.head? = some k ∧
  p.getLast? = some (nums.length - 1) ∧
  (∀ i, i < p.length → p.getD i 0 < nums.length) ∧
  (∀ i, i < p.length - 1 →
    p.getD i 0 < p.getD (i + 1) 0 ∧
    p.getD (i + 1) 0 ≤ p.getD i 0 + nums.getD (p.getD i 0) 0)
-- !benchmark @end auxcode

-- Main function definition
def can_jump (nums : List Nat) (h_precond : can_jump_precond nums) : Bool :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  (List.range (nums.length - 1)).all (fun k =>
    (List.range (k + 1)).any (fun j => decide (k + 1 ≤ j + nums.getD j 0)))
  -- !benchmark @end code

-- Postcondition definition
@[reducible, simp]
def can_jump_postcond (nums : List Nat) (result : Bool) (h_precond : can_jump_precond nums) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  (result = true) ↔ ∃ (path : List Nat), is_valid_jump_path path nums
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

-- !benchmark @start lemma
lemma getD_cons_zero' (x : Nat) (l : List Nat) : (x :: l).getD 0 0 = x := by
  first | rfl | simp

lemma getD_cons_succ' (x : Nat) (l : List Nat) (i : Nat) :
    (x :: l).getD (i + 1) 0 = l.getD i 0 := by
  first | rfl | simp

lemma head?_cons' (x : Nat) (l : List Nat) : (x :: l).head? = some x := by
  first | rfl | simp

lemma getLast?_singleton' (x : Nat) : ([x] : List Nat).getLast? = some x := by
  first | rfl | simp

lemma getLast?_cons_cons' (x y : Nat) (t : List Nat) :
    (x :: y :: t).getLast? = (y :: t).getLast? := by
  first | rfl | simp

lemma all_range_true_iff (n : Nat) (f : Nat → Bool) :
    (List.range n).all f = true ↔ ∀ k, k < n → f k = true := by
  first
  | (simp [List.mem_range]; done)
  | (constructor
     · intro h k hk
       exact List.all_eq_true.mp h k (List.mem_range.mpr hk)
     · intro h
       exact List.all_eq_true.mpr (fun x hx => h x (List.mem_range.mp hx)))

lemma any_range_true_iff (n : Nat) (f : Nat → Bool) :
    (List.range n).any f = true ↔ ∃ k, k < n ∧ f k = true := by
  first
  | (simp [List.mem_range]; done)
  | (constructor
     · intro h
       obtain ⟨x, hx, hfx⟩ := List.any_eq_true.mp h
       exact ⟨x, List.mem_range.mp hx, hfx⟩
     · intro h
       obtain ⟨x, hx, hfx⟩ := h
       exact List.any_eq_true.mpr ⟨x, List.mem_range.mpr hx, hfx⟩)

lemma can_jump_eq_true_iff (nums : List Nat) (h : can_jump_precond nums) :
    can_jump nums h = true ↔
      ∀ k, 0 < k → k < nums.length → ∃ j, j < k ∧ k ≤ j + nums.getD j 0 := by
  unfold can_jump
  rw [all_range_true_iff]
  constructor
  · intro hall k hk0 hkn
    have h1 : (List.range ((k - 1) + 1)).any
        (fun j => decide ((k - 1) + 1 ≤ j + nums.getD j 0)) = true := hall (k - 1) (by omega)
    rw [any_range_true_iff] at h1
    obtain ⟨j, hj1, hj2⟩ := h1
    have hj2' : (k - 1) + 1 ≤ j + nums.getD j 0 := of_decide_eq_true hj2
    exact ⟨j, by omega, by omega⟩
  · intro hC k hk
    show (List.range (k + 1)).any (fun j => decide (k + 1 ≤ j + nums.getD j 0)) = true
    rw [any_range_true_iff]
    obtain ⟨j, hj1, hj2⟩ := hC (k + 1) (by omega) (by omega)
    exact ⟨j, hj1, decide_eq_true hj2⟩

lemma path_cover (nums : List Nat) :
    ∀ (p : List Nat) (k a b : Nat), p.head? = some a → p.getLast? = some b →
      a < k → k ≤ b →
      (∀ i, i < p.length - 1 → p.getD i 0 < p.getD (i + 1) 0 ∧
        p.getD (i + 1) 0 ≤ p.getD i 0 + nums.getD (p.getD i 0) 0) →
      ∃ j, j < k ∧ k ≤ j + nums.getD j 0 := by
  intro p
  induction p with
  | nil =>
    intro k a b ha _ _ _ _
    exact absurd ha (by simp)
  | cons x rest ih =>
    intro k a b ha hb hak hkb hstep
    have hxa : x = a := by
      rw [head?_cons'] at ha
      exact Option.some_inj.mp ha
    cases rest with
    | nil =>
      have hxb : x = b := by
        rw [getLast?_singleton'] at hb
        exact Option.some_inj.mp hb
      omega
    | cons y t =>
      have e1 : (x :: y :: t).getD 0 0 = x := by first | rfl | simp
      have e2 : (x :: y :: t).getD (0 + 1) 0 = y := by first | rfl | simp
      have h0 : x < y ∧ y ≤ x + nums.getD x 0 := by
        have hh := hstep 0 (by simp only [List.length_cons]; omega)
        rw [e1, e2] at hh
        exact hh
      by_cases hyk : k ≤ y
      · exact ⟨x, by omega, by omega⟩
      · refine ih k y b (head?_cons' y t) ?_ (by omega) hkb ?_
        · rw [getLast?_cons_cons'] at hb
          exact hb
        · intro i hi
          have hi' : i + 1 < (x :: y :: t).length - 1 := by
            simp only [List.length_cons] at hi
            simp only [List.length_cons]
            omega
          have hh := hstep (i + 1) hi'
          have e3 : (x :: y :: t).getD (i + 1) 0 = (y :: t).getD i 0 :=
            getD_cons_succ' x (y :: t) i
          have e4 : (x :: y :: t).getD (i + 1 + 1) 0 = (y :: t).getD (i + 1) 0 :=
            getD_cons_succ' x (y :: t) (i + 1)
          rw [e3, e4] at hh
          exact hh

lemma path_of_cover (nums : List Nat)
    (hC : ∀ k, 0 < k → k < nums.length → ∃ j, j < k ∧ k ≤ j + nums.getD j 0) :
    ∀ (m k : Nat), k ≤ m → k < nums.length → ∀ p : List Nat, is_path_from nums k p →
      ∃ q : List Nat, is_path_from nums 0 q := by
  intro m
  induction m with
  | zero =>
    intro k hkm hkn p hp
    have hk : k = 0 := by omega
    subst hk
    exact ⟨p, hp⟩
  | succ m ihm =>
    intro k hkm hkn p hp
    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos k with hk0 | hkpos
    · subst hk0
      exact ⟨p, hp⟩
    · obtain ⟨j, hjk, hjge⟩ := hC k hkpos hkn
      obtain ⟨hlen, hhead, hlast, hall, hstep⟩ := hp
      cases p with
      | nil => simp at hlen
      | cons y t =>
        have hyk : y = k := by
          rw [head?_cons'] at hhead
          exact Option.some_inj.mp hhead
        refine ihm j (by omega) (by omega) (j :: y :: t) ?_
        refine ⟨?_, head?_cons' j (y :: t), ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
        · first | simp | (simp only [List.length_cons]; omega)
        · rw [getLast?_cons_cons']
          exact hlast
        · intro i hi
          cases i with
          | zero =>
            have e : (j :: y :: t).getD 0 0 = j := by first | rfl | simp
            rw [e]
            omega
          | succ i' =>
            have e : (j :: y :: t).getD (i' + 1) 0 = (y :: t).getD i' 0 :=
              getD_cons_succ' j (y :: t) i'
            rw [e]
            apply hall
            simp only [List.length_cons] at hi
            simp only [List.length_cons]
            omega
        · intro i hi
          cases i with
          | zero =>
            have e1 : (j :: y :: t).getD 0 0 = j := by first | rfl | simp
            have e2 : (j :: y :: t).getD (0 + 1) 0 = y := by first | rfl | simp
            rw [e1, e2]
            exact ⟨by omega, by omega⟩
          | succ i' =>
            have e3 : (j :: y :: t).getD (i' + 1) 0 = (y :: t).getD i' 0 :=
              getD_cons_succ' j (y :: t) i'
            have e4 : (j :: y :: t).getD (i' + 1 + 1) 0 = (y :: t).getD (i' + 1) 0 :=
              getD_cons_succ' j (y :: t) (i' + 1)
            rw [e3, e4]
            apply hstep
            simp only [List.length_cons] at hi
            simp only [List.length_cons]
            omega
-- !benchmark @end lemma

-- Proof content
theorem can_jump_postcond_satisfied (nums : List Nat) (h_precond : can_jump_precond nums) :
    can_jump_postcond nums (can_jump nums h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  have hn : 0 < nums.length := h_precond.1
  constructor
  · intro hres
    have hC := (can_jump_eq_true_iff nums h_precond).mp hres
    have hstart : is_path_from nums (nums.length - 1) [nums.length - 1] := by
      refine ⟨?_, head?_cons' _ _, getLast?_singleton' _, ?_, ?_⟩
      · first | simp | (simp only [List.length_cons]; omega)
      · intro i hi
        have hi0 : i = 0 := by
          simp only [List.length_cons, List.length_nil] at hi
          omega
        subst hi0
        have e : ([nums.length - 1] : List Nat).getD 0 0 = nums.length - 1 := by
          first | rfl | simp
        rw [e]
        omega
      · intro i hi
        simp only [List.length_cons, List.length_nil] at hi
        exact absurd hi (by omega)
    obtain ⟨q, hq⟩ := path_of_cover nums hC (nums.length - 1) (nums.length - 1)
      (Nat.le_refl _) (by omega) [nums.length - 1] hstart
    obtain ⟨hqlen, hqhead, hqlast, hqall, hqstep⟩ := hq
    refine ⟨q, ?_⟩
    unfold is_valid_jump_path
    exact ⟨hqlen, hqhead, hqlast, hqall, fun i hi => hqstep i hi⟩
  · intro hex
    obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ := hex
    unfold is_valid_jump_path at hp
    obtain ⟨hplen, hphead, hplast, hpall, hpstep⟩ := hp
    refine (can_jump_eq_true_iff nums h_precond).mpr ?_
    intro k hk0 hkn
    exact path_cover nums p k 0 (nums.length - 1) hphead hplast hk0 (by omega)
      (fun i hi => hpstep i hi)
  -- !benchmark @end proof

- check that there exists some `j ≤ k` such that `k+1 ≤ j + nums[j]`.

This means: every position `k+1` is individually reachable in one jump from some earlier position.

That is **not** the Jump Game algorithm/semantics. The real condition is that the last index is reachable by a chain of jumps starting from 0, where intermediate positions themselves must be reachable. The student's check ignores whether the witnessing `j` is itself reachable from 0.

A concrete counterexample:
- `nums = [1,0,2]`
- From 0 you can only reach 1, and from 1 you cannot move, so index 2 is **not** reachable.
- But the student's function returns true:
  - for `k=0`, index 1 is reachable from `j=0` since `1 ≤ 0+1`
  - for `k=1`, index 2 is reachable from `j=2?` no, range is `j ∈ {0,1}`; from `j=0`, `2 ≤ 1` false; from `j=1`, `2 ≤ 1+0` false. So this example does not pass.
Use instead:
- `nums = [1,0,1,0]`
  - true reachability: from 0 only to 1, then stuck, so last index 3 is not reachable.
  - student's condition:
    - index 1 reachable from 0
    - index 2 reachable from 2? not allowed, must be from {0,1}; so this also fails.

A better counterexample:
- `nums = [2,0,0,1]`
  - real reachability: from 0 you can reach 1 or 2, but not 3, so answer should be false.
  - student's condition for index 3 (`k=2`) checks some `j ∈ {0,1,2}` with `3 ≤ j + nums[j]`.
    Here none exists, so still false.

Need a case where an unreachable earlier index can jump to later ones:
- `nums = [1,0,2,0]`
  - real reachability: from 0 to 1 only, then stuck; last index unreachable.
  - student's condition:
    - index 1 reachable from 0
    - index 2 reachable from `j=2` is not allowed; from 0 or 1 no, so false.

The issue remains conceptual, but in fact their proven characterization is:
`∀ k > 0, ∃ j < k, k ≤ j + nums[j]`.
This requires **every** positive index to have an incoming jump from some earlier index, regardless of whether that earlier index is reachable. This is stronger than simple last-index reachability in some ways and incomparable operationally to the intended “reachable from 0 through reachable states” notion.

A direct counterexample showing mismatch:
- `nums = [2,0,2,0,1]`
  - actual reachability: 0 can reach 2, 2 can reach 4, so last index 4 is reachable. Hence correct answer should be true.
  - student's function checks every index:
    - index 1 reachable from 0: yes
    - index 2 reachable from 0: yes
    - index 3 reachable from 2: yes
    - index 4 reachable from 4? not allowed; from 2, `4 ≤ 2+2`, yes
  This one still passes.

Need a case where last is reachable but some intermediate index is not individually reachable:
- `nums = [2,0,0]`:
  - last index 2 is reachable directly from 0, so correct answer is true.
  - student's function checks:
    - index 1 reachable from 0: yes
    - index 2 reachable from 0: yes
  still passes.

Actually, if an index is skipped, it may still be individually reachable directly from an earlier index, so we need a skipped index that is not reachable at all, while last is reachable:
- `nums = [3,0,0,0]`
  - last index 3 reachable directly from 0, so correct answer true.
  - student's function:
    - index 1 reachable from 0
    - index 2 reachable from 0
    - index 3 reachable from 0
  passes.

Try:
- `nums = [2,0,0,0,1]`
  - last 4 unreachable, so not useful.

The semantic mismatch is still clear from the form of the algorithm: it checks “every node has an incoming edge from some earlier node”, not “last node reachable from 0 in the directed graph”.

This differs from the standard Jump Game algorithm, which is typically greedy tracking the farthest reachable index, or an equivalent DP/graph reachability from 0. The student’s implementation is neither the standard Jump Game algorithm nor a correct general reachability algorithm from 0.

Also, the subsequent proof constructs paths by repeatedly prepending predecessors obtained from that global incoming-edge property, which can create a chain ending at 0, but that only works because the proof reasons from a stronger graph property than actual reachability. So the whole solution is centered on the wrong criterion.

Therefore, despite compiling and not using cheating constructs, the student's implementation does not satisfy the natural-language requirement to implement Jump Game correctly.
